quests.instruction: At Meera’s school, the Class 10 students are called seniors. A Class 6 student who has only just joined is a ___ student.
quests.hint: Who has been at the school for the shortest time?
quests.explanation: Senior means older or higher in rank. Junior means younger or lower in rank.
quests.funFact: In many schools, older students are paired with younger buddies to help them settle in.

quests.instruction: Meena put far too much sugar in the lemonade, so it tasted too sweet. To fix it, she squeezed in extra lemon, which made it taste more…
quests.hint: Sugar makes lemonade sweet; a certain fruit takes that taste away.
quests.explanation: Sugar gives a sweet taste, and lemon juice does the opposite. Adding more lemon moves the flavor toward sour.
quests.funFact: Lemons contain citric acid, which gives them their sharp taste.

quests.instruction: When the teacher called the register, Tina answered, “Present!” Her desk-mate was ill and stayed at home, so he was marked…
quests.hint: The register has a name for children who aren’t there.
quests.explanation: Present means being at a place. Absent means not being there.
quests.funFact: “Present” can also mean a gift or the current time, as well as being here.

quests.instruction: The washing hung on the line all morning in the hot wind. By noon, even the thick towels that had dripped at breakfast were…
quests.hint: What does hot wind do to damp cloth?
quests.explanation: Washing starts out wet and dries as the water evaporates. Hot wind speeds that up.
quests.funFact: Hot, windy days dry washing fastest because the water evaporates quickly.

quests.instruction: The word “child” names one person. The word “children” names more than one. We call the second kind…
quests.hint: Mouse and mice: one names a single thing, the other names more.
quests.explanation: Singular means just one. Plural means more than one.
quests.funFact: Some English plurals are irregular, like mouse–mice and foot–feet.

quests.instruction: On the first day of the school fair, hundreds of visitors came. On rainy Monday, only a ___ turned up.
quests.hint: A rainy Monday brings only a small number of visitors.
quests.explanation: Many means a large number. Few means just a small number.
quests.funFact: Fairs have been held for centuries, and some medieval fairs lasted for weeks.

quests.instruction: Wearing the school uniform on Monday is compulsory. Bringing a toy for Friday’s show-and-tell is ___, since you can choose.
quests.hint: Which one can you decide not to do?
quests.explanation: Compulsory means you must do it. Optional means it’s up to you.
quests.funFact: “Compulsory” comes from a Latin word meaning “to drive” or “to force”.

quests.instruction: The queue at the ticket counter stretched out of the door all morning. By evening, it was so ___ that only two people were waiting.
quests.hint: Look at the queue in the morning, then again in the evening.
quests.explanation: A long queue has many people in a stretch. When most have gone, the queue becomes short.
quests.funFact: In American English, a queue is usually called a line.

quests.instruction: The letters A, B and C are capital letters, also called uppercase. The small versions, a, b and c, are…
quests.hint: Capital letters are large; their partners are smaller.
quests.explanation: Uppercase letters are the large capitals. Lowercase letters are the smaller ones.
quests.funFact: The terms come from old printing shops, where capital letters were kept in the upper drawer of the type case.

quests.instruction: Dad’s kite caught the strong wind and soared way up into the sky, but my kite stayed ___ near the ground.
quests.hint: Which kite stayed close to the grass?
quests.explanation: High means far above the ground, and low means close to it.
quests.funFact: Kites have been flown in China for more than two thousand years.

quests.instruction: When Dad says, “Let’s eat something,” he’s being general. When he says, “Let’s have vegetable biryani at the corner café,” he’s being…
quests.hint: “Let’s eat something” is vague. Look for the sentence with details.
quests.explanation: A general statement is broad and doesn’t give details. A specific one names exactly what is meant.
quests.funFact: “Specific” comes from a Latin word meaning “of a particular kind”.

quests.instruction: In July, many children in the north of the world are enjoying summer holidays. At the same time, children in Australia are bundling up for…
quests.hint: Think of the southern half of the world in July.
quests.explanation: The north and south halves of the world have opposite seasons. When it’s summer in the north, it’s winter in the south.
quests.funFact: Some Australians have a barbecue on the beach on Christmas Day.

quests.instruction: A ruler can measure your height exactly: 132 cm. If you simply say, “About a metre and a bit,” that’s a ___ guess.
quests.hint: Which answer gives you every centimetre?
quests.explanation: An exact answer is precise. A rough answer is only close.
quests.funFact: Scientists use very exact tools to measure tiny things, like the width of a human hair.

quests.instruction: The wooden toy boat bobbed on top of the bath water. When Neel dropped the metal key into the tub, it dropped straight to the bottom. Keys can’t…
quests.hint: The boat stayed on top of the water. Think about what the key did instead.
quests.explanation: Floating means staying on top of the water. A key sinks because it’s denser than water.
quests.funFact: Things float if they are less dense than the liquid they’re in.

quests.instruction: Hari faces the rising sun every morning. At the end of the day, the sun disappears behind the houses on the opposite side, in the…
quests.hint: At the end of the day, the sun sets in the opposite direction from where it rose.
quests.explanation: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west. East and west are opposite directions on a compass.
quests.funFact: A compass rose shows north, south, east and west.

quests.instruction: The class pet hamster escaped under the cupboard. Meera, not afraid at all, reached in and fished him out. Her friend stayed far back, too ___ to help.
quests.hint: Who kept her distance from the cupboard?
quests.explanation: Meera showed bravery. Her friend’s fear was the opposite reaction: scared.
quests.funFact: Hamsters are mostly active in the evening and at night.

quests.instruction: The door of the corner shop swings inward, toward you. The fire-exit doors at the cinema swing ___ so a crowd can push through fast.
quests.hint: Picture a crowd rushing toward the doors.
quests.explanation: Inward means toward the inside. Outward means toward the outside.
quests.funFact: Emergency exit doors in public buildings often open outward so crowds can leave quickly.

quests.instruction: Maya wrote, “The Sun is a planet,” in her notes. Her teacher marked it with a cross because the statement was…
quests.hint: A cross on a correct fact would be a mistake; here the fact isn’t correct.
quests.explanation: The Sun is a star, not a planet, so the statement doesn’t match the facts. That makes it false.
quests.funFact: The Sun holds almost all of the mass in our solar system.

quests.instruction: After a night of only three hours’ sleep, Chitra yawned all through class. After a full ten hours, her sister bounced out of bed feeling…
quests.hint: Who is ready for a game of tag?
quests.explanation: Too little sleep leaves you tired. Plenty of rest leaves you full of energy.
quests.funFact: Short naps of twenty to thirty minutes can help people feel more alert.

quests.instruction: The climbers stood on the peak, the very top of the mountain. The village far below, tucked between the hills, sits in the…
quests.hint: Between two hills, the land dips low.
quests.explanation: A peak is the highest point. A valley is the low land between hills or mountains.
quests.funFact: The Himalayas have many deep valleys between their high peaks.

quests.instruction: The class was cheerful all week. On the day their favorite teacher said goodbye on her last day, even the loudest children felt…
quests.hint: Saying goodbye to a favorite teacher brings a certain feeling.
quests.explanation: Cheerful moods are a kind of happiness. Saying goodbye to someone you like brings the opposite feeling: sad.
quests.funFact: People can feel happy and sad at the same moment, such as when saying goodbye after a wonderful trip.

quests.instruction: Mira rubbed sandpaper over the wooden spoon again and again. At first it felt splintery, but when she finished, it felt…
quests.hint: What does sanding do to wood?
quests.explanation: Sanding wears away bumps, so the wood becomes smooth instead of rough.
quests.funFact: Sandpaper is graded by numbers: the bigger the number, the finer the grit.

quests.instruction: The ferry leaves a small town and chugs toward a tiny island. The big stretch of land connected to the rest of the continent is called the…
quests.hint: Look for the one that sits on solid land, not in water.
quests.explanation: An island is land surrounded by water. The mainland is the large body of land joined to a continent.
quests.funFact: Greenland is the largest island in the world that isn’t a continent.

quests.instruction: A woodcutter’s axe must be sharp. After he accidentally chopped a stone, the edge became ___ and barely cut the log.
quests.hint: Think of metal hitting a hard stone.
quests.explanation: A sharp edge cuts easily. When the edge is worn down, it becomes blunt.
quests.funFact: Woodcutters keep axes sharp with a stone called a whetstone.

quests.instruction: In the family photo, Grandpa and Grandma sat in the front row. The tall cousins stood in the ___ row.
quests.hint: Who gets seen best if the tall people stand behind?
quests.explanation: The front row is closest to the camera. The back row is the row behind.
quests.funFact: Photographers often arrange group photos by height so that everyone’s face can be seen.

quests.instruction: A synonym is a word with the same meaning, like “big” and “large”. A word with the opposite meaning, like “big” and “small”, is called an…
quests.hint: Think of a word that starts like “anti”, which means against.
quests.explanation: Synonyms are words that mean the same thing. Antonyms are words that mean the opposite.
quests.funFact: “Antonym” comes from Greek words meaning “against” and “name”.

quests.instruction: Dev made a good decision when he returned the lost wallet. Keeping the money would have been a ___ decision.
quests.hint: Think about whose wallet it was and what the right thing to do is.
quests.explanation: Returning something that isn’t yours is the right thing to do. Keeping it would be the opposite of good.
quests.funFact: Many cities have lost-property offices where lost wallets and phones can be returned.

quests.instruction: The post office is on the left side of the street as you walk toward the market. On the walk home, with the market behind you, it will be on your…
quests.hint: Turn around: which side switches?
quests.explanation: When you turn around, left and right swap. A building on your left becomes a building on your right.
quests.funFact: In India and the UK, cars drive on the left side of the road; in many other countries, they drive on the right.

quests.instruction: Dad put the lightest plates at the top of the stack. The heaviest ones, which hold up the whole pile, go at the…
quests.hint: A heavy base holds up everything above it.
quests.explanation: The top is the highest layer. The bottom is the lowest layer, and it carries the weight above it.
quests.funFact: Pyramids are built with wide bases because a broad bottom makes a structure stable.

quests.instruction: The sofa cushions sank under Ravi. The wooden bench in the park didn’t give at all. It was…
quests.hint: Compare a bench with a cushion under your hand.
quests.explanation: Soft things give way when pressed. Hard things don’t.
quests.funFact: Balsa wood is one of the softest, lightest woods, while oak is very hard.
